messages:
jess: Hey team — multiple EU customers reporting huge tail latency and intermittent 401s since ~06:10 UTC. One example request id: req_0a1b2c. They say traffic looks like it was routed to us-west even though region pin is eu-west. Any quick theories?

lucy: Looking now. I can see a surge in eu-west queues at 06:08 and our autospill policy started routing overflow to us-west around 06:09. 401s could be due to token audience mismatch if requests crossed regions.

matt-oncall: I'm seeing routing logs that show a lot of fallback events. Also auth-service in eu reported some "unknown key" errors around the same time. Could be KMS/key propagation + spillover combo.

arun-infra: Confirmed: KMS rotation completed at 06:05, but some inference shards were backpressured and didn't pull the new keyset before the surge. When routing spilled requests to different region, token audiences didn't match the keys there -> 401s.

jess: Ugh. Customer also flagged an unexpected billing/egress note. They saw a small spike in cross-region traffic cost. Can we quantify?

lucy: Quick mitigation applied: pinned active sessions for high-value customers to eu-west to avoid cross-region routing for ~10m. Command: `routing.pin(session_id, region=eu-west, ttl=10m)`

support-bot: pinned 230 sessions for eu-west at 06:20 UTC. :white_check_mark:

matt-oncall: Repro snippet (from routing logs):
```
route_event: spillover
from: eu-west
to: us-west
session: sess-87
request_id: req_0a1b2c
token_aud: eu-west-only
auth_err: token_aud_mismatch
```

arun-infra: Plan: deploy a routing hotfix to (1) avoid changing token audience on fallback, (2) add a token-proxy rewrite when cross-region forward is unavoidable, and (3) add guard so KMS rotations require shards to confirm key pull before being fully active. Hotfix v2.1.3 pushed to routing nodes in eu and is in canary.

lucy: TL;DR: root cause is capacity exhaustion in eu leading to automatic spillover. That exposed a timing window where KMS rotation + stale keysets + sticky session routing caused 401s and extra cross-region egress.

jess: Thanks. What about repro steps we can send to the customer so they can verify fix?

matt-oncall: Repro steps for support playbook: 1) Trigger small burst against eu endpoint with header `X-Region: eu-west`. 2) Force eviction by simulating queue saturation (we have a test-mode). 3) Observe routing logs for `spillover` events and check `auth_err` field. 4) Confirm requests for the same session do not change audience when hotfix applied.

finance-bot: Billing team alerted. Preliminary estimate: ~12k cross-region requests during the incident window; we'll follow up with exact egress cost and any customer credits needed.

arun-infra: Hotfix is live in eu canary groups, rolling to 60% now. Monitoring p50/p99 latency and auth-err counts. Keeping detailed logs for 24h.

lucy: Post-mortem action items: add KMS-rotation canary requiring shard confirmation, update routing fallback to preserve or rewrite token audience safely, add alert for pending key pulls > 30s, and add an integration test that simulates spillover + rotation.

jess: Appreciate the quick response. Please add a brief timeline and what we tell the customer after you have the final numbers. :heart:

support-bot: incident escalated -> eng-runtime + infra. Case #INC-2026-479 created.

matt-oncall: I'll follow up with timeline and link to logs once rollout completes.

arun-infra: Keeping the channel updated.

jess: Thanks all.
